job: Turn employee proposals into funded, measured experiments and portfolio decisions
current_workaround: Idea forms, slides and separate project trackers
record: Experiment portfolio with hypothesis, budget and outcome decisions
wedge: Explicit experiment evidence and follow-through rather than popularity-ranked idea collection
why_pay: Hypothesis: Make funded experiments accountable and reduce forgotten initiatives
expansion: Cross-division portfolio and partner innovation programs

competitors.name: Brightidea
competitors.facts: Innovation software spans challenges, idea evaluation and portfolio outcomes.
competitors.price: No numeric public subscription price verified; sales-led offering.

pricing.unit: organization/month; proposed USD, scope-capped pilot plan
pricing.free_boundary: 14-day trial with synthetic data
pricing.paid_boundary: Team workflows, guest collaboration, history and exports
pricing.lifetime: No unlimited hosted lifetime plan; an offline template/export pack could be sold separately, with no MRR credit.

channel: Proposed: innovation consultants already running corporate programs
retention: Program cycles and funded experiment reviews
moat: Hypothesis: Organization-specific outcome history, contingent on sustained sponsorship
mvp: Roles, audit history, import/export and backup recovery

cost.assumptions: Engineering estimate for 3–5 small design-partner accounts, not a measured quote; labor, tax, payment fees, acquisition and audits excluded. Pilot quota hypothesis: maximum five organizations, 250 active cases, 10000 structured child records, 2GB aggregate attachments, 20MB per file and 2000 transactional emails/month; no bulk marketing, video or uncapped AI. Exceeding a cap pauses new imports pending repricing; these limits are not measured capacity results.
cost.drivers: Bound document storage, email and exports; no paid AI in core.
cost.revenue_stage: Up to $300/month could fund managed database/backups, monitoring and bounded integrations after paying usage; not enterprise service levels.

risks: Discretionary budget
Large-company sales requirements
Generic project tools suffice without a durable program
global_limits: Global workflow; employee participation rules and confidential IP vary
validation: Replay a completed program and ask three sponsors to fund the next cycle at $299/month
kill_gate: Stop if no sustained program owner or recurring budget exists
score_rationale: Analyst judgment: recurrence and budget reflect the workflow; distribution/wedge discount established alternatives. Security and integration scope constrain feasibility.
source_limit: Vendor features and price do not prove an underserved segment, our conversion, revenue, or retention.

review.reason: The existing scores already discount discretionary budgets and weak differentiation. No extra penalty. A 200–2000-person organization may impose enterprise onboarding despite low infrastructure cost, and consultants may deliver the value themselves. Recurring funded experiments and a continuing sponsor must exist before software scope is justified; idea collection without measured stop/continue decisions does not satisfy this product thesis.

name: Deal due-diligence workspaces
buyer: Boutique transaction adviser managing several overlapping company sales
job: Coordinate controlled diligence requests, document versions and review decisions
current_workaround: Virtual data room plus email and a request spreadsheet
record: Transaction diligence request linked to controlled documents and Q&A
wedge: Advisor-led request workflow layered over customer-owned secure storage; no transaction marketplace
why_pay: Hypothesis: Reduce repeated document chasing across active transactions
expansion: Reusable diligence templates and adviser portfolio coordination

competitors.facts: Virtual data room includes diligence checklists, document controls and Q&A; capabilities depend on plan.
competitors.price: Request pricing; no numeric public amount verified.

pricing.free_boundary: 14-day trial with synthetic data
pricing.paid_boundary: Team workflows, guest collaboration, history and exports
pricing.lifetime: No unlimited hosted lifetime plan; an offline template/export pack could be sold separately, with no MRR credit.

channel: Proposed: boutique M&A advisers using approved synthetic transaction packs
retention: Overlapping transactions, though a single company may buy only once
moat: Hypothesis: Request and diligence evidence history; strong existing secure-room competitors
mvp: Roles, audit history, import/export and backup recovery

cost.assumptions: Engineering estimate for 3–5 small design-partner accounts, not a measured quote; labor, tax, payment fees, acquisition and audits excluded. Pilot quota hypothesis: maximum five organizations, 250 active cases, 10000 structured child records, 2GB aggregate attachments, 20MB per file and 2000 transactional emails/month; no bulk marketing, video or uncapped AI. Exceeding a cap pauses new imports pending repricing; these limits are not measured capacity results.
cost.drivers: Controlled access, storage and independent security review; prefer existing customer storage, professional reviews excluded.
cost.revenue_stage: Up to $300/month could fund managed database/backups, monitoring and bounded integrations after paying usage; not enterprise service levels.

risks: Event-driven revenue at end buyer
Enterprise security expectations
Established data rooms bundle workflows
global_limits: No legal or investment advice; data residency, transaction confidentiality and competition restrictions vary
validation: Replay one anonymized closed deal; test an adviser-level multi-deal subscription
kill_gate: Stop if demand is only one-time rooms or certified secure storage must be supplied by us
score_rationale: Analyst judgment: recurrence and budget reflect the workflow; distribution/wedge discount established alternatives. Security and integration scope constrain feasibility.
source_limit: Vendor features and price do not prove an underserved segment, our conversion, revenue, or retention.

review.reason: Existing VDRs already bundle request workflows, and base scores capture trust, episodic demand and weak acquisition. No extra deduction. Customer-owned storage reduces custody but does not solve permission drift, document-version references or Q&A visibility. An adviser-level portfolio is the plausible recurring buyer; one successful deal replay cannot establish adviser retention or acceptable procurement/security requirements.
